options.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Direction name: Context Bar.
Create a realistic production-quality UI design for Guides, an existing native macOS desktop overlay used by a front-end developer to manually measure and annotate visible interfaces. This is a redesign exploration, not a web dashboard or a marketing slide.
Input images: Image 1 is the user's current overcrowded toolbar, for product identity and controls; image 2 is the current overlay for ruler/measurement identity. Both are visual references, not edit targets. Existing project codebase /Volumes/Projects/guides, visual tokens: opaque charcoal #1F1F22, hot pink #FF1487 selection, quiet white secondary text, 14px panel corners, 7px controls. Keep that visual language, improve hierarchy and usability.
Target dimensions: a natural 1440 x 1024 desktop app frame. One single coherent screen, no multi-option collage, no device frame, no design presentation headings, no explanatory arrows outside the UI. A generic pale neutral browser documentation page is visible underneath the overlay, to demonstrate this is a utility on top of other apps; do not copy private document text. Background is quiet and secondary.
Hero use case: Annotate is active and Rectangle is chosen; a pink outlined rectangle highlights an interface button on the underlying page. The desktop remains live. Keep spotlight switched off in this frame so the image remains bright.
Layout strategy: a compact opaque charcoal floating top toolbar with purposeful horizontal spacing, roughly 1120px wide, 56px high, inset 30px from top, centered; no giant app container. It contains a subtle drag grip; a small 'Guides' product label; a clear segmented control with icon-and-text choices 'Guides', 'Area', 'Annotate' (Annotate is pink selected); an icon-and-text 'Tools' dropdown; quiet undo/redo icons; and a clearly separated text action 'Pin & work' with pin icon, followed by 'Hide'. Main toolbar must feel composed and short, with three groups and no confusing unlabeled icons.
Directly underneath, one SHORT contextual annotation strip about 650px wide shows 'Select', 'Arrow', 'Line', and 'Rectangle' with Rectangle visibly selected by a subtle tint and pink icon, then a single pink colour well and a 'Style' dropdown. Show no rainbow swatch inventory, no redundant scale/unit controls in Annotate, no disabled Delete/Clear clutter. Style controls are progressive disclosure.
A very small anchored contextual popover near the selected rectangle titled 'Rectangle' shows only: 'Outline' with a pink colour well and '2 pt' stroke control; a row 'Spotlight' with an off switch and a quiet hint 'Dim outside this rectangle'; and one quiet 'Delete rectangle' action. This is compact and purposeful, not cards nested inside cards.
At the bottom center a small charcoal hint bar reads 'Annotating · Drag to draw · Esc to hide' using discreet keycaps. Adjacent to Pin & work the understandable secondary wording 'Click through to your app' can appear as tiny one-line supporting copy if it fits naturally. Use generous breathing room within compact controls, readable 14-16px SF-style typography, accessible contrast, crisp realistic line icons, beautiful alignment and precise spacing. At most one pink filled choice on the main toolbar. Selected rectangle has small circular white handles with pink edges. No ruler when annotating, no fake CSS inspection, no capture/export buttons, no future tools, no sidebars, no gradients, no glass wallpaper tint, no excessive shadows. All controls and panels fit inside the frame with no truncation. Prioritize clear hierarchy over showing every feature.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Direction name: Tool Dock.
Create a realistic production-quality UI design for Guides, an existing native macOS utility that floats over other apps for manual screen measurement and annotation. This exploration deliberately replaces the long horizontal toolbar with a compact vertical tool dock and one contextual inspector. It is a desktop overlay, not a dashboard or a website.
Input images: Image 1 is the actual current crowded toolbar; image 2 is the existing overlay with pink measurements and light rulers. Use these as product identity references, not literal edit targets. Existing project /Volumes/Projects/guides; palette opaque charcoal #1F1F22, accent #FF1487, high contrast white text, round 14px panels and 7px controls. Preserve the established neutral charcoal-and-pink identity.
Target dimensions: 1440 x 1024, a single coherent desktop screen. No collage, presentation captions, option numbers, phone, device frame, promotional graphics or giant outer app card. Show a generic very pale browser documentation page as the underlying app, with a quiet component example and a primary button near the center. This page is simply a work surface, all Guides UI floats above it.
Layout and hero use case: Annotate is active, Rectangle is the selected annotation tool, and a pink rectangle with white circular pink-rimmed handles frames a button in the center of the underlying app. Spotlight is off. No rulers in annotation mode.
At left, inset 24px, a narrow floating charcoal vertical dock about 92px wide, 560px high, starts below the top browser chrome. Its top is a tiny drag grip and subtle Guides monogram. Beneath, three generous stacked icon-and-label mode buttons 'Guides', 'Area', 'Annotate'. Annotate has a pink selected background, other buttons neutral. All labels legible, do not use unexplained unlabeled icons. A subtle divider, then an icon-and-label 'Tools' launcher. At the bottom, a 'Hide' action with icon. Dock occupies little space, no full-height navigation sidebar.
At upper right floats a contextual charcoal inspector, approximately 270px wide, no more than 425px high. Title 'Annotate'. One row of four shape buttons with visible labels 'Select', 'Arrow', 'Line', 'Rectangle', arranged as two rows of two if needed for readable spacing. Rectangle subtly selected. Beneath a light divider show 'Rectangle style', then labelled compact rows 'Colour' with a pink colour well, 'Stroke' with '2 pt', 'Spotlight' with off toggle and one quiet line 'Dim outside the rectangle'. Do not display a big rainbow palette, unrelated scale/rem controls, measurements, future annotation tools or permission settings. Bottom row contains compact undo/redo controls and 'Delete' action. Clean sections defined by spacing, no nested cards.
At bottom center a small independent charcoal bar, roughly 440px wide, shows the explicit action 'Pin & work' with a pin icon and supporting line 'Keep marks visible. Click through to your app.' This is the clear next action after drawing; style it as the primary action by size and placement with a restrained pink outline or pink icon, leaving the strongest filled pink on the active dock button. Include a quiet 'Esc Hide' key hint to the right.
Create beautiful, restrained native macOS utility aesthetics: SF-style typography 14-16px, precise iconography, balanced spacing, readable labels, opaque neutral dark surfaces, white text, subtle separator lines, very light shadows. Most of the underlying app stays unobstructed. No gradients, wallpaper tint, glass panels, unnecessary badges, metrics, profile features, capture/export or CSS-inspection claims. One focused annotation workflow, simple choices, no clipped content.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Direction name: Floating Palette.
Create a realistic, production-quality redesign of Guides, an existing native macOS desktop overlay for manual measurement and annotation. Explore one compact movable tool palette that brings the active task, settings and finish action into one place. This must be substantially different from a long toolbar or a left dock plus a right inspector.
Input images: Image 1 is the user's actual overcrowded two-row toolbar, reference for real features and charcoal/pink identity; Image 2 is the current measurement overlay, reference for pink canvas outlines and contrast. These are inspiration references, not edit targets. Existing project /Volumes/Projects/guides, tokens charcoal #1F1F22, pink #FF1487, secondary white at 64%, panels 14px radius and controls 7px. Keep these established native visual traits.
Target dimensions: 1440 x 1024, one focused desktop app frame, no multiple concepts, no explanatory design slide, no option label. The underlying app is a quiet pale browser documentation page with a primary button around the center-right. It is only the background work surface; Guides is an overlay and must not look like a web dashboard.
Layout: one beautiful opaque charcoal floating utility palette in the upper-left quadrant at x80 y130, about 360px wide and 490px tall. Everything needed for the current annotation task lives in this one palette. No top floating toolbar, no full-height sidebar, no distant inspector, no extra floating cards.
Palette hierarchy: a compact header row with a small drag grip, 'Guides', an unobtrusive icon-and-text 'Tools' dropdown and a close/hide icon. Below, a generously spaced segmented mode row 'Guides', 'Area', 'Annotate', with Annotate selected pink. Then heading 'Draw a shape', followed by four equally sized icon-and-text buttons in a single row or two rows: 'Select', 'Arrow', 'Line', 'Rectangle'. Rectangle has a restrained pink tint to show subordinate selection without competing with main mode.
Under a thin divider show a short inline settings section with readable labels: 'Outline' with pink colour well and '2 pt' dropdown; 'Spotlight' with off toggle. One small secondary line says 'Dim outside the rectangle'. No rainbow row and no calibration/units clutter while annotating. No invented text/ellipse tools or capture features.
Bottom of palette: a quiet row of 'Undo', 'Redo' and 'Delete' actions. Then a full-width clear high-emphasis button labelled 'Pin & work' with pin icon, using a light neutral high-contrast fill so the pink accent remains focused on selected mode. Beneath it the calm description 'Keep marks visible and use your app'. A very small footer 'Esc to hide'. Close the hierarchy clearly without cards inside cards.
Canvas: a pink outlined rectangle with small white circular handles frames the button in the underlying page, positioned well clear of the palette. Spotlight is off. The rest of the desktop is clean, without rulers in annotation mode. A tiny quiet anchored hint near the rectangle may say 'Drag handles to resize' but avoid redundant tool instructions.
Rendering: refined SF-style native typography, 14-16px body labels with very clear contrast, 18px header, crisp line icons, careful alignment, warm professional restraint, purposeful whitespace within a compact utility. Soft controlled shadows, neutral opaque surfaces, no wallpaper tinted glass, no gradients, no decorative images or big product logo, no charts, no metrics, no accounts, no future roadmap features. Keep all controls legible and fully inside the palette; if crowded simplify spacing rather than clipping labels. The purpose is to make choosing a tool, styling it and returning to the underlying app feel obvious.
